mainTopic: Dating a גט by officials, changed names in a גט, penalties for צרות who remarried, and the scribe who mixed up the גט and the receipt
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה: the strict rules about a wrongly dated גט belong to רבי מאיר, while the חכמים accept even a date by a minor city official. רבה rules that a גט dated by the governor of בשכר is valid even for רבי מאיר, because naming a senior official honors the kingdom, while naming a minor one insults it. רב adds that the חכמים say the child is כשר, but they agree he is a ממזר if the names of the people or their cities were changed, and רב אשי proves this from the משנה. Next the גמרא discusses the צרות who married when they should have waited for יבום. It asks whether the משנה's word 'married' excludes illicit relations, which bears on רב המנונא's ruling, and it brings two versions of this discussion. It then explains why the משנה needs both of its cases of penalized צרות. Finally it turns to the scribe who mixed up the גט and the receipt. שמואל and רב אדא בר אהבה disagree about what רבי אליעזר means by 'immediately.' The amud ends with a challenge to שמואל from the משנה's mention of a 'second' husband.

steps.title: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר about how a גט is dated
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends. The strict rulings about a wrongly dated גט belong to רבי מאיר. The חכמים say she is divorced even if the date follows a local city official.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the opinion of רבי מאיר. But the חכמים say: even if he only wrote the date in the name of the guardsman of the city, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the משנה. It tells us that the strict rule just stated is only רבי מאיר's view, and the חכמים are much more lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the משנה, a גט dated the 'wrong' way, such as by the wrong kingdom, was treated harshly. Now we learn that this harshness is רבי מאיר's view alone. For the חכמים, how the date is counted does not affect whether the גט works. Even dating it by a minor local official is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the opinion of רבי מאיר (and not everyone's)
A guardsman or minor local official

steps.confusionAlert: 'זו דברי רבי מאיר' looks back at the earlier strict rules in the משנה. It does not start a new rule. It tells you who said the earlier part.

phrases.english: This is the statement of רבי מאיר,
but the Sages say:
even if he wrote only
in the name of the guardsman in the city
phrases.notes: He means he dated the גט by the years of this local official.

phrases.english: she is divorced.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר, אֲבָל חֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the משנה that began on an earlier amud by naming who holds the strict view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The strict rules about dating are רבי מאיר's. The חכמים hold that a גט dated even by a minor city official is valid.

steps.title: A real גט dated by the governor of בשכר
steps.stepSummary: A גט was dated by the years of the governor of בשכר. רב נחמן בר רב חסדא sent the question to רבה: what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain גט in which the date was written in the name of the governor of בשכר. רב נחמן בר רב חסדא sent it before רבה: in a case like this, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells of a real case. A question about it is sent to רבה, and this sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is where this case fits in the argument of the משנה. A governor is a local official, a bit like the סנטר, but he is much more important. So does רבי מאיר's strictness apply here?

keyTerms.meaning: A certain גט (introduces a real case)
He sent it before (a question sent to a greater authority)
In a case like this, what is the law?

phrases.english: There was a certain bill of divorce in which was written
in the name of the governor of בשכר,

phrases.aramaic: שַׁלְחֵהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא
phrases.english: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא sent it
before רבה:
In a case like this, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the argument of the משנה to a real case that falls between its examples.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is a גט dated by the governor of בשכר valid, even according to רבי מאיר?

steps.title: רבה rules that even רבי מאיר agrees the גט is valid
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that here even רבי מאיר agrees the גט is valid, because the governor belongs to that same kingdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent back: in this case even רבי מאיר agrees. Why? The governor is from that same kingdom.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question. The גט is valid according to everyone, even רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's concern is about the kingdom. A governor is an official of the ruling kingdom, so dating by him is in effect dating by that kingdom. That is why רבי מאיר has no problem with it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי מאיר's strictness is not about using local officials in general. It is about honoring the ruling kingdom.

phrases.english: He sent to him:
phrases.notes: רבה is sending his answer back to רב נחמן בר רב חסדא.

phrases.english: In this case, even רבי מאיר concedes,
What is the reason?
He is from that kingdom.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ: בְּהָא אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי מֵאִיר מוֹדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question sent in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The גט is valid even according to רבי מאיר, because the governor is an official of the ruling kingdom.

steps.title: How is a governor different from the city guardsman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a governor should be different from the סנטר. The סנטר is also an official of the kingdom, yet רבי מאיר does not accept him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is this different from the guardsman in the city?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה's reason. The city guardsman also works for the kingdom, yet only the חכמים accept a גט dated by him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implies that רבי מאיר rejects dating by the סנטר. If 'he is from that kingdom' were enough, the סנטר would pass too. So רבה's reason seems too broad.

phrases.english: And what is different from the guardsman in the city?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason רבה gave in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reason that a governor is 'from that kingdom'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סנטר is also from the kingdom, yet the משנה implies that רבי מאיר rejects him. So belonging to the kingdom cannot be the deciding factor.

steps.title: A minor official insults the kingdom, but a governor honors it
steps.stepSummary: Dating by a minor guardsman is demeaning to the kingdom. Dating by a senior governor is complimentary to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is demeaning to them. Here, it is complimentary to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to how the kingdom would feel about each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real test is honor, not simply belonging to the kingdom. Dating by a lowly guardsman makes the kingdom look small. Dating by a senior governor shows the kingdom respect, so even רבי מאיר accepts it.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר's concern is the honor of the ruling kingdom. A date by a senior governor honors the kingdom, so it is valid. A date by a minor guardsman insults the kingdom, so רבי מאיר rejects it. The חכמים accept both.

phrases.english: There, the matter is demeaning for them,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the guardsman case and 'them' is the ruling kingdom.

phrases.english: here, the matter is complimentary for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases by the honor or insult to the kingdom
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any official of the kingdom should be treated the same, so the governor and the guardsman should have the same law.
steps.terutzMaskana: What matters is whether the kingdom is honored or insulted. The governor honors it, and the guardsman insults it.

steps.title: רב: only רבי מאיר makes the child a ממזר, but the חכמים agree when names are changed
steps.stepSummary: רב teaches that the ruling that the child is a ממזר follows רבי מאיר. The חכמים say the child is כשר, but they agree he is a ממזר if the names of the people or their cities were changed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא, who said in the name of רב: This is the view of רבי מאיר. But the חכמים say the child is fit. And the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר that if he changed his name or her name, or the name of his city or her city, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב tells us who holds the strict rule that the child is a ממזר. He also gives one case where even the חכמים agree with that strict rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 already showed that the strict rules of the משנה follow רבי מאיר. רב now applies this to the child as well: the חכמים say the child is כשר. A wrong date is only a small mistake, but changing the names of the people or their cities is a basic mistake, so even the חכמים hold the child is a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: The child born from her second marriage
Fit, with no flaw in his lineage
A child born from a forbidden relationship, who may not marry into the general community

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the dispute is only about small mistakes in a גט. When the mistake touches who is divorcing whom, everyone agrees the גט fails.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said that Rav said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Meir,
but the Rabbis say: the child is fit.
And the Rabbis agree with Rabbi Meir
that if he changed his name or her name,
or the name of his city or the name of her city,
then the child is a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side question about the governor of בשכר to the main dispute in the משנה, now about the child's status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The child is a ממזר only according to רבי מאיר. The חכמים say he is כשר, except when the names of the people or their cities were changed, where all agree he is a ממזר.

steps.title: רב אשי brings support from the משנה's case of changed names
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the משנה itself also teaches that changing the names gets the full set of penalties.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: We also learned this in the משנה: If he changed his name or her name, or the name of his city or her city, she must leave this husband and that husband, and all these penalties apply to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי quotes a line from the משנה that seems to support what רב just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the case of changed names separately and gives it all the strict penalties. If this line follows the חכמים, then it backs up רב: even the חכמים are strict when names are changed. The next step proves who this line follows.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this, a phrase that brings support from a משנה or ברייתא
She must leave both this man and that man

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
We too have also learned this:
If he changed his name or her name,
or the name of his city or the name of her city,
she must leave this one and that one,
and all these ways apply to her.
phrases.notes: "These ways" is the list of penalties the משנה gave earlier for a woman who remarried with a bad גט.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, אַף אֲנַן נָמֵי תְּנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support from the משנה for the second half of רב's statement.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים agree the child is a ממזר when names are changed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The line in the משנה about changing his name, her name, or the names of their cities.

steps.title: This line cannot follow רבי מאיר, or it would be listed together with the earlier cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the author of the changed-names line is. If it were רבי מאיר, the משנה would have listed it together with the wrong-date case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who teaches this? If you say רבי מאיר, then let the משנה combine the cases and teach them together!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks who the author of the changed-names line is, so it can finish רב אשי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is strict both about a wrong date and about changed names, so for him the two cases have the same law. If this line were his, the משנה would have put them in one list. Since it lists the changed-names case separately, it must belong to someone who treats it differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the author of this teaching?
Let him combine them and teach them together

phrases.english: Who teaches this?
If you say it is Rabbi Meir,
let him combine them and teach them together!
phrases.notes: He means the wrong-date cases and the changed-names case, which would have the same law for רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַאן קָתָנֵי לַהּ? אִילֵּימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the author of the line רב אשי quoted, to complete his proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the changed-names line is not רבי מאיר's.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The fact that the משנה lists the changed-names case separately instead of combining it with the earlier cases.

steps.title: So the line follows the חכמים, and רב is proven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the changed-names line follows the חכמים, so even they are strict in that case, just as רב said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that it is the חכמים. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof: the line follows the חכמים, so רב's statement is confirmed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the line is not רבי מאיר's, it must be the חכמים'. They give the full penalties when names are changed, which is exactly what רב said they agree to. The repeated "שמע מינה" means the proof is accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, meaning this is proven
The Rabbis, the same as the חכמים

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים are lenient about a wrong date, but if the names of the people or their cities are changed, everyone agrees she must leave both men and the child is a ממזר.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it that it is the Rabbis;
yes, learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ רַבָּנַן; שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the reasoning in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The changed-names line in the משנה follows the חכמים, which proves רב: the חכמים agree with רבי מאיר when names are changed.

steps.title: New line of the משנה: the law speaks of marrying, not of illicit relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about the צרות of עריות and notes that it says they married. That suggests the penalties apply only if they married, not if they had illicit relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: "All the עריות that they said, and so on." If they married, yes. If they had illicit relations, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic in the משנה and points out a detail in its wording. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the צרות "married" other men. From that word, the גמרא infers that the penalties apply only to marriage. If the צרות had illicit relations without marrying, the penalties would not apply. The next step will examine this inference.
steps.confusionAlert: The phrase "married, yes; illicit relations, no" is not a final ruling. It is only what the wording of the משנה seems to imply, and the גמרא is about to look into it.

phrases.english: "All the forbidden relatives that they said, etc."
If they married, yes;
if they had illicit relations, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, based on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From its wording, the משנה's penalties seem to apply only if the צרות married, not if they had illicit relations.

steps.title: Does the משנה refute רב המנונא?
steps.stepSummary: If the penalties apply only when the צרות married, then a שומרת יבם who merely had illicit relations would not be forbidden to her יבם. That seems to contradict רב המנונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is a refutation of רב המנונא, who said: a שומרת יבם who had illicit relations is forbidden to her יבם!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the inference from step 10 ('only if they married') and uses it to challenge רב המנונא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צרות in the משנה turn out to have been waiting for יבום all along, so they were שומרות יבם when they married someone else. If only marriage brings the penalties, including being forbidden to the יבם, then illicit relations alone would not forbid her. רב המנונא says illicit relations do forbid her, so the משנה seems to argue with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say. It opens a suggestion the גמרא is testing.
A refutation, a strong challenge that would knock out an opinion.
A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום or חליצה.

phrases.english: Let us say this is a refutation of Rav Hamnuna,
as Rav Hamnuna said:
A woman waiting for her yavam who had illicit relations
is forbidden to her yavam!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference from step 10 to challenge an outside ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's ruling that a שומרת יבם who had illicit relations is forbidden to her יבם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives the penalties only for marriage, which implies illicit relations alone do not forbid her to the יבם. That contradicts רב המנונא.

steps.title: 'Married' is just the polite way of saying it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the refutation. The same law applies to illicit relations. The משנה wrote 'married' only because it prefers refined language.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The משנה says 'they married,' and the same is true if they had illicit relations. It said 'married' because it chose a nicer way of speaking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on step 11 and says the משנה is not limiting the law to marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference in step 10 depended on reading 'married' as a precise limit. Here the גמרא says the word was picked for politeness, not to exclude illicit relations. So nothing in the משנה argues with רב המנונא.

keyTerms.meaning: The same law applies to another case.

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying illicit relations are fine. It simply avoids describing an ugly case, and the law is the same.

phrases.english: No; the משנה says 'they married,'
and the same is true if they had illicit relations.
And the fact that it teaches 'they married'
is because it used refined language.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the refutation raised in step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the inference that the משנה limits the penalties to actual marriage.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'married' was chosen for politeness, not as a precise limit, so it cannot be used to exclude illicit relations.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא's principle that a משנה may choose polite wording without meaning to limit the law.

steps.title: A second version: 'married' includes illicit relations
steps.stepSummary: Some tell the discussion differently. They start by assuming that 'married' in the משנה also covers illicit relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: 'they married,' and the same is true if they had illicit relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the discussion. This line sets up the next step, which asks what follows from this reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the reading 'married includes illicit relations' came only as a defense against a refutation. In this version it is the starting point. That turns the משנה from a possible problem for רב המנונא into a possible support.

phrases.english: And some say:
'they married,' and the same is true if they had illicit relations;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the discussion from steps 10 through 12 with a different starting reading of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, the משנה's 'they married' is read from the start as including illicit relations.

steps.title: Maybe the משנה supports רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: If illicit relations count like marriage, then the משנה seems to back רב המנונא: a שומרת יבם who had illicit relations is forbidden to her יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports רב המנונא, who said: a שומרת יבם who had illicit relations is forbidden to her יבם?
steps.whatsHappening: Based on the second version's reading, the גמרא suggests the משנה is a proof for רב המנונא. Its answer to this suggestion comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids the צרות to the יבם after they married. If illicit relations are the same as marrying, the משנה would teach exactly רב המנונא's ruling. The 'לימא' wording signals the גמרא is only testing this proof, not accepting it yet.

keyTerms.meaning: Supports. It points to a source that helps an opinion.
To her יבם, her late husband's brother.

phrases.english: Let us say it supports Rav Hamnuna,
as Rav Hamnuna said:
A woman waiting for her yavam who had illicit relations
is forbidden to her yavam?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a suggested proof from the reading given in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: רב המנונא's ruling that a שומרת יבם who had illicit relations is forbidden to her יבם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the צרות who married, read as including illicit relations, where the penalties include being forbidden to the יבם.

steps.title: Only marrying counts, because it looks like the overseas-husband case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof for רב המנונא: the משנה really means 'married' and not illicit relations, because a remarried woman can be confused with an אשה שהלך בעלה למדינת הים.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is specifically when they married, because that case can be confused with a woman whose husband went overseas.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 14. It says the word 'married' in the משנה is meant exactly, not as polite wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who remarried looks just like a woman whose husband went overseas and she remarried, where חכמים gave heavy penalties. So חכמים gave the same penalties here. Illicit relations do not look like that case, so the משנה gives no proof for רב המנונא.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman whose husband went overseas (and she remarried, thinking he died)

steps.whatToRemember: In this version of the discussion, the penalties apply only when the צרה actually married. They do not apply after illicit relations, so the משנה is no proof for רב המנונא.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 12 said 'married' was just refined language. This is the second version of the discussion, and here 'married' is meant exactly. Don't mix up the two versions.

phrases.english: No;
specifically when they married,
because it can be confused
with a woman whose husband went to a country overseas.
phrases.notes: In that case she remarried and the first husband came back. She is penalized and must leave both men.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof for רב המנונא given in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that 'married' includes illicit relations, so the proof from the משנה falls away.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed 'married' was loose wording. Really it is exact, because only marriage looks like the overseas-husband case that the penalty is based on.

steps.title: Quoting the next case in the משנה and saying it is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of הכונס את יבמתו and says this case is needed even though it looks like the earlier case.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One who marries his יבמה, etc.' And it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and says both cases are needed. This is a setup line; the next two steps explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught penalties for צרות in two similar cases. In the first, the ערוה turned out to be an איילונית. In this one, the יבם married his יבמה, another צרה married someone else, and then the יבמה turned out to be an איילונית. A reader might ask why the משנה needs both, so the גמרא says 'צריכא': each one teaches something.

keyTerms.meaning: one who marries his יבמה (his brother's widow)
it is necessary (both cases must be taught)
etc.: the rest of the quote from the משנה

phrases.english: 'One who marries his yevama, etc.'
phrases.notes: The full line: her צרה married another man, then the יבמה was found to be an איילונית, so the צרה must leave both men.

phrases.english: And it is necessary;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה needs both cases of penalizing צרות; neither one is extra.

steps.title: Why the first case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had taught only the first case, we might think the penalty is because no יבום happened at all. Where יבום did happen, we might think there is no penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it had taught us only the first case, I would say the penalty is because the מצוה of יבום was not fulfilled. But here, where the מצוה of יבום was fulfilled, I might say no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of why both cases are needed. The second case teaches something the first case could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case nobody did יבום at all, so the צרה's remarriage looks very wrong. In the second case the יבם did marry the יבמה, so the מצוה seemed done, and the other צרה seems free to remarry. Without the second case, we might say she is not penalized.

keyTerms.meaning: the מצוה of marrying a brother's widow
I might say no (the law would not apply)

phrases.english: For if it had taught us only that first case –
phrases.notes: The first case is the צרות of a ערוה who married, and the ערוה turned out to be an איילונית.

phrases.english: [I would say the penalty is] because the מצוה of yibbum was not fulfilled;
but here –
where the מצוה of yibbum was fulfilled,
I might say no [penalty];

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first reason behind the 'צריכא' of step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the משנה need the case of הכונס את יבמתו if it already taught the first case?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the first case alone, we might have tied the penalty to the fact that no יבום happened. So we would not penalize where יבום was done.

steps.title: Why the second case alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה had taught only the second case, we might think the penalty is because the צרה was available to the יבם. In the first case, where she was not available to him, we might think there is no penalty. So both are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had taught us only here, I would say the penalty is because she was placed before him. But there, where she was not placed before him, I might say no. So it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other half: the first case teaches something the second case could not. It finishes by saying both cases are necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second case, the יבם could have done יבום with any of the wives, so this צרה should have waited before remarrying. That is a good reason to penalize her. In the first case the צרות seemed fully free of יבום, so she had no reason to wait, and we might not penalize her. Each case has its own reason someone might go easy, so the משנה teaches both.

keyTerms.meaning: she was placed before him (available to the יבם for יבום)

steps.whatToRemember: Two cases, two possible reasons to go easy. Case 1 (צרת ערוה): she was never available for יבום. Case 2 (הכונס את יבמתו): the מצוה of יבום seemed done. The משנה teaches the penalty in both.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only here –
[I would say the penalty is] because she was placed before him;
phrases.notes: He could have chosen her for יבום, so she should have waited before remarrying.

phrases.english: but there –
where she was not placed before him,
phrases.notes: In the first case, as the ערוה's צרה, she seemed free of יבום altogether.

phrases.english: I might say no [penalty];
[therefore both are] necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the 'צריכא' argument from the other side and closes it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the second case alone, we might have tied the penalty to her being available to the יבם. So we would not penalize in the first case, where she was not available.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both cases in the משנה are needed. Each one blocks a different reason someone might think the צרה is not penalized.

steps.title: The משנה's case of the scribe who mixed up the papers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a scribe wrongly gave the גט to the wife and the receipt to the husband, and רבי אליעזר rules based on whether the גט came out 'immediately.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The scribe wrote and made a mistake. He gave the גט to the woman and the receipt to the man, and so on. רבי אליעזר says: if it turned up immediately, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה's case of the mixed-up papers. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the papers were mixed up, the wife handed the גט to the husband instead of the husband giving it to her. If the גט is found in the husband's hand, we have to decide whether a real divorce ever happened. רבי אליעזר says the answer depends on timing: 'immediately' or 'after some time.'

keyTerms.meaning: The scribe who writes the גט
A receipt, showing the wife was paid her כתובה

phrases.english: The scribe wrote and made a mistake,
and gave the גט to the woman and the receipt, etc.;
phrases.notes: The receipt went to the husband. So the wife ended up handing the גט to him, which is backwards.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If it came out immediately, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Came out' means the גט turned up in the husband's hand. If so, it is not a valid divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתַב הַסּוֹפֵר וְטָעָה, וְנָתַן גֵּט לָאִשָּׁה וְשׁוֹבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section of the משנה, separate from the יבם discussion in steps 10-18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, whether the divorce is valid depends on whether the גט was found in the husband's hand 'immediately' or 'after some time.'

steps.title: What counts as 'immediately' and what counts as 'after some time'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact meaning of the two time terms in רבי אליעזר's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of 'immediately,' and what is the case of 'after some time'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי אליעזר's two time words actually mean. This sets up two different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's whole ruling depends on timing, but the משנה never says how much time is 'immediately.' The גמרא needs a clear line so we know when the divorce is valid and when it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?

phrases.english: What is the case of 'immediately,'
and what is the case of 'after some time'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of the key words in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where the line falls between 'immediately' and 'after some time.'

steps.title: שמואל: 'immediately' means while they are still sitting and dealing with the divorce
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says 'immediately' is as long as everyone is still sitting and busy with the divorce. Once they get up, it is 'after some time.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: as long as they are sitting and busy with this matter, it is 'immediately.' Once they got up, it is 'after some time.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the first answer. The line is whether the divorce meeting is still going on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While everyone is still there, finding the גט in the husband's hand clearly comes from the mix-up, so there was no real divorce. Once the meeting has ended, we assume the divorce was done properly and the גט was later given back to him. This is a very short time window.

keyTerms.meaning: They got up, meaning the meeting ended

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
As long as they are sitting
and busy with that same matter,
this is 'immediately';
once they got up, this is 'after some time.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Immediately' means while the divorce meeting is still going on. Once they get up, it is 'after some time.'

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: 'immediately' means before she has remarried
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה says that as long as she has not remarried, it is 'immediately.' Once she has remarried, it is 'after some time.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said: if she has not remarried, it is 'immediately.' If she has remarried, it is 'after some time.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer. He draws the line at whether she has married someone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב אדא בר אהבה, the window is much longer than for שמואל. Until she remarries, the problem can still be fixed by having the husband give the גט properly. Once she has a new husband, we do not undo her marriage.

phrases.english: And Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
if she has not remarried, this is 'immediately';
if she has remarried, this is 'after some time.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 20 that disagrees with שמואל in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The line is remarriage. Before she remarries it is 'immediately'; after she remarries it is 'after some time.'
steps.whyThisMatters: The two answers set up the challenge in the next step, which tests each one against the משנה's wording.

steps.title: The משנה mentions a 'second' husband, which fits רב אדא but seems hard for שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the first husband cannot destroy the rights of the second. That fits רב אדא, who speaks of remarriage. But according to שמואל, where is there a second husband?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: the first husband does not have the power to destroy the rights of the second. This works well for רב אדא בר אהבה, which is why it says 'second.' But according to שמואל, what is the 'second'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל from the משנה's wording. The words 'second husband' seem to fit only רב אדא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא's 'after some time' is exactly the case where she has remarried, so a 'second husband' fits perfectly. שמואל's 'after some time' starts as soon as the meeting ends, when there is usually no second husband yet. So why would the משנה talk about protecting a second husband?

keyTerms.meaning: It is not in his power

phrases.english: We learned:
It is not in the power of the first husband
to destroy the rights of the second.
Granted, according to Rav Adda bar Ahava,
that is why it teaches 'second,'
but according to Shmuel, what is the 'second'?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: לֹא כׇּל הֵימֶנּוּ מִן הָרִאשׁוֹן לְאַבֵּד זְכוּתוֹ שֶׁל שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the two definitions from steps 21-22 against the wording of the משנה and attacks שמואל's.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's definition of 'after some time' from step 21.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה talks about protecting a 'second husband,' which assumes she has remarried. In שמואל's 'after some time,' there is usually no second husband yet, so the משנה's wording does not seem to match him.
